purpose: Determine whether the Brown et al. (2010) CMOR 3D wavelet survey can be transferred faithfully to the available SonotaCo catalogue scale without weakening its published support and temporal-linking requirements.

reference.title: A meteoroid stream survey using the Canadian Meteor Orbit Radar II: Identification of minor showers using a 3D wavelet transform

classification: source-grounded feasibility audit; not a scientific comparator result

published_design.catalogue_scale: approximately three million CMOR orbits stacked across seven years into one virtual year
published_design.coordinates: Sun-centered ecliptic radiant longitude and latitude plus geocentric speed
published_design.annual_background: recursive annual median after removing values more than three standard deviations above the median
published_design.refinement: repeat near linked maxima using steps five times smaller while retaining the same probes

sonotaco_2025_feasibility_audit.archive: exact checksum-pinned SonotaCo 2025 archive already used for comparator development
sonotaco_2025_feasibility_audit.quality_filter: reuse the frozen Sugar-paper catalogue quality filter only to define a conservative complete-vector universe: Qc > 15 deg, Vg <= 75 km/s, Vg uncertainty <= 0.1 Vg + 1 km/s
computed_quantities: counts in each one-degree solar-longitude bin
median, p90, p95, p99, and maximum one-degree-bin count
number and fraction of bins with at least 300 total radiants
maximum possible number of three-bin temporal chains in which every bin reaches 300 total radiants

decision_rule.faithful_single_year_supported: Only if the annual catalogue provides broad three-bin temporal support at the published 300-radiant floor; this audit still cannot reproduce the paper's seven-year virtual-year stacking or CMOR exposure model.
decision_rule.no_relaxation: Do not lower the 300-radiant floor, shorten the three-point chain, enlarge time bins, evaluate only known shower coordinates, or call a reduced wavelet core a faithful Brown et al. reproduction after seeing this audit.

claim_boundary: A negative feasibility result means the published CMOR survey is not fairly executable on one SonotaCo year. It is not evidence that the wavelet method performs poorly, and it is not a win for OrbitTrace.
